grammar.title: 特殊疑问句
grammar.tip: 特殊疑问句用 what、who、which、where、when、why、whose、how 开头，不能用 Yes 或 No 回答，问什么就答什么：Where do you meet after school? — At the park. 句型：疑问词 + be + 主语（Who is your new friend?），或 疑问词 + do/does + 主语 + 动词原形（What does she like doing?）。注意：What is she like? 问性格，What does she look like? 问长相。

units.notes:
I checked the word list against book/unit1.json with a script. It has all 27 words and then all 17 phrases, once each, in book order and with exact spelling. No item is marked understandOnly. The script also confirmed: no repeated Chinese meaning, no repeated emoji, no zh longer than 8 characters, 16 sentences and 12 dialogues.

Fixes applied:
- grammar.tip: now lists which, and gives the two question patterns: wh-word + be + subject, and wh-word + do/does + subject + base verb. The two example patterns come from the book's own short pattern list.
- watch over: changed to 守护. The two reviewers gave different fixes. I used the 'must' fix (守护 only) instead of 守护；看护, because 看护 would still overlap with 照顾 (take care of) in the pick-the-meaning question.
- rise is now （太阳）升起 and rise into is now 升入空中. 入 hints at 'into' in 看图说英语, and the two options no longer look the same.
- sents[2]: the two reviewers suggested different replacements. I chose 'Which class is your best friend in?' over 'What is your new classmate good at?'. It removes the copy of dlgs[5] and also adds a which-sentence. Tiles keep their capital letters (game.js tokens), so 'Which' clearly goes first, and the word order is fixed.
- sents[3]: now 'I am glad you are my friend.', which removes the copy of dlgs[2] and finally puts glad in a sentence.
- sents[6]: added 'so much' so that 'best' cannot move to the end.
- sents[12]: removed 'always', which could also move.
- dlgs[10]: the reply is now 'The nurse will take care of it.' The game spells the building 'Monster Center' everywhere, so the line avoids the name instead of spelling it a second way. The child also says 'take care of' aloud.
- dlgs[11]: now a which-question, 'Which subject do you want to improve?' The 'Yes, I want to improve it.' distractor shows the yes/no mistake that the grammar point warns about.

Two extra changes for the same reasons:
- sents[4]: removed 'usually'. 'Where do you go after school usually' would also be acceptable English, and the exact-order checker would mark it wrong. This is the same issue as sents[6] and sents[12].
- dlgs[1]: the reply is now 'He has short dark hair.' (it was 'He is of medium height.'). Otherwise 'dark' was never spoken in any sentence or reply. Medium height is still practised in sents[9] and in Daisy's chat words. The wrong replies, 'He is honest and kind.' (personality) and 'He is good at maths.', are still clearly wrong for a look-like question.

Question words now covered:
- Sentences: who, what, which, where, when, why and how.
- Dialogues: 11 of the 12 lines are Wh-questions (what, who, where, when, whose, why, which). dlgs[0] and dlgs[1] still test the difference between 'What is he like?' and 'What does he look like?'.

Echo Island appears in sents[12], dlgs[10] and Daisy's persona. Everything else is real school life. The boss Ollie (牵手海獭) and the chat name Daisy are not used anywhere else in the game's JS files (checked with grep).

Emoji: 🪞 appearance (Unicode 13) and 🪑 (Unicode 12) are the newest. If they show as empty boxes on the phone, use 🖼️ for appearance and 🔁 for take somebody's place.

units.key: What is your school life like?

grammar.title: 一般现在时
grammar.tip: 说每天、经常做的事用一般现在时。主语是第三人称单数（he、she、it，或一个人、一样东西）时，动词加 -s 或 -es（gets、watches、studies），have 变 has；问句和否定句用 does / doesn't，后面的动词用原形。说频率用 always、usually、often、never，问频率用 How often。例：She gets up at six. Does he walk to school?

units.notes:
Final Unit 2 (School life). Checked by script against book/unit2.json: words has all 29 words and 13 phrases (42 items), exactly once each, in book order, with exact spelling. All 42 emoji are different and no two Chinese meanings are the same. There are 16 sents (6 to 9 words each, no repeated word inside a sentence, no commas inside) and 12 dlgs (every correct reply is 10 words or fewer). I also ran the game's own scoring code (norm, scoreSpeech and bestScore copied from game.js) on every boss dialogue. The correct reply beats both wrong replies by at least 15 points, even when the first or second word is dropped. The old dialogue 4 tied 85 to 85 in that test; the new one does not.

FIXES APPLIED
(1) grammar.tip rewritten (must). It now covers it and singular things as subjects, -s/-es with gets, watches, studies and have to has, does/doesn't followed by the base verb, the frequency adverbs and How often. It is three sentences instead of two because the rule needs that much to be accurate.
(2) sents[8] is now 'Maths helps me develop the skills to solve problems.' / 数学帮我培养解决问题的能力。 I used the English reviewer's version over the game reviewer's art-club version because it has only one valid order and still uses solve, develop and skill.
(3) sents[11] is now 'I keep a diary in English.' / 我用英语记日记。 The game reviewer's 'English diary every day' version is also unambiguous, but 'keep a diary' already means doing it regularly, so 'every day' added nothing.
(4) Third-person sound and spelling coverage. sents[10] is now 'Our school day finishes at half past four.' (/ɪz/). sents[12] is now 'My cousin studies hard at junior high school.' (-ies). I also changed sents[2] to 'Our class has geography twice a week.' / 我们班每周上两次地理课。 This adds has, which neither reviewer covered, and gives an it-type singular subject. The sentences now have /s/ (gets, takes, helps, puts, picks, packs), /z/ (goes, reads, studies, has) and /ɪz/ (finishes). look forward to stays in dlgs[9] and the talk words. daily life is still in the word list and the talk topic.
(5) teen is now 青少年的（形容词）, the game reviewer's fix. It is 9 characters, one over the ideal 8, but it shows the part of speech so the teen/teenager pair is fair. The 看图说英语 problem is still open: if the child says teen for 🧑 青少年, it scores low. Engine suggestion: add noMix:[['teen','teenager']] and have distract() skip that pair.
(6) pack is now 打包；装进包里, so it no longer overlaps with clean up = 打扫干净. The sentence translation 收拾好书包 stays because it is the natural Chinese for that sentence.
(7) dlgs[3] wrong replies are now 'Yes, my mum often cooks.' and 'Yes, they are at home now.'
(8) The boss is now 🐝 蜜蜂老师 Miss Bee (14 words), because the 🐙 八爪博士 island boss already exists. 🐝 is not used by any of the 13 island bosses in data.js. I could not see the other textbook units' bosses, so check 🐝 against Units 1 and 3 to 8 when merging.
(9) The Kai label is corrected. Dialogue 5 uses Kai, the player's shy friend from the adventure (STORY.md: 小凯, whom the player helps catch his first monster), not a rival.

FIXES CHANGED OR REJECTED
(a) 'get ... ready for'. The two reviewers disagree. The English reviewer wants to rename it 'get something ready for'. I rejected that because the schema requires the exact official spelling, and it would no longer match the book list. I kept the official spelling and took the game reviewer's engine fix instead. Action needed in D:/Claude/echo-island/game.js makeQ: for the word types lw, ls and sr_w, set q.audio = it[0].replace(/\s*(?:\.\.\.|…)\s*/g, ' ') so the TTS, the Youdao fallback and the clip generator all say 'get ready for'. Spoken scoring already ignores the dots (norm() strips non-letters). Until that patch lands, this one entry still sends '...' to the TTS.
(b) Talk character. Ruby was dropped as both reviewers asked (it is a Pokémon game-version name, and 'Ruby' is also in world.js TRAINER_NAMES). I did not use the suggested 'Ella': isles/c-circus-clock-party.js already has the trainer 'Early Bird Ella', a schoolgirl who talks about getting up early and going to bed at nine, which is the same topic and would confuse. The new name is Alice (新同学爱丽丝). It appears nowhere in the codebase (I searched all .js and .md files).

OTHER NOTES
sents[9] 'Our drama club puts on a show every term' could in theory also be built as 'puts a show on'. Because the child hears the audio first and 'puts on a show' is the standard textbook form, I judged the risk low and kept it. Official items not used in any sentence or dialogue (they are still in the word list): corner, teenager, greeting, sincerely, realize, luckily, just, presentation, mood, rocky, get ... ready for, daily life. The three understand-only words (sincerely, presentation, mood) stay in book order. Validation scripts: C:/Users/Frank/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--Claude/073ac0e8-fd7f-4d6a-954a-c072b256e3ed/scratchpad/u2/chk.js and sim2.js.

units.key: What do you know about the seasons?

grammar.title: 形容词

units.notes:
Source: scratchpad/book/unit3.json (The seasons; grammar = adjectives). Checked by script: words has all 38 official items (30 words + 8 phrases), each once, in book order, exact spelling (sandcastle and crop are understandOnly but included). There are 16 sents and 12 dlgs. No emoji repeats within the unit, and none matches an emoji in data.js or in the finished Unit 1 (scratchpad/u1_final.json).

Reviewer fixes applied: (1) MUST, clear: changed to 晴朗无云的 with 🌌, so it no longer matches sunny ☀️ 晴朗的. (2) MUST, sents[8]: changed to "Our town is very peaceful on winter evenings." / 冬天的晚上，我们小镇非常宁静。 (3) SHOULD, sents[10]: changed to "The four seasons follow the same order every year." / 四季每年都按同样的顺序更替。 This makes the fact correct, drops the Unit 8 word "pattern", and still uses follow in the book's sense. (4) SHOULD, part: changed to 地区；区域 with 🧩. (5) SHOULD, take a trip: changed to ✈️.

Partly rejected: for wet, I agree 💦 must go, but the suggested 🌧️ is already used for ['rainy','下雨的','🌧️'] (data.js line 279). A child would be primed to say "rainy". I used 💧 潮湿的 instead.

Extra changes from the same collision check: gather 🍎→🌰 (🍎 is fruit in data.js). alive 🌱→🐣 (🌱 is biology). solar term 🗓️→🌞 (🗓️ is month). sandy 🏖️→🏜️ (🏖️ is beach). through ⏳→↔️ (⏳ is wait in data.js and patient in Unit 1). follow 🔄→➡️ (🔄 is come and go in Unit 1). feature ✨→🔍 (✨ is come along in Unit 1). be based on 🧱→🏗️ (🧱 is basic in Unit 1). play an important part in 🔑→🎭 (🔑 is key in data.js; 🎭 also suggests "play a part").

sents[0] changed from "The weather gets wet in early summer." to "It gets very wet in early summer." / 初夏时节天气变得很潮湿。 The old tiles could also make "The weather in early summer gets wet", which starts with the same capitalised tile. The checker (game.js onLoCheck) accepts only the exact order, so that version would be marked wrong. The new sentence still practises get + adjective.

Repeated tiles (we/We, The/the) are safe because the checker compares in lower case.

Coverage: every official word or phrase appears in at least one sentence or dialogue. In dialogues: feature, south, loudly, article, decide, crop, culture, in fact, take a trip, work one's land. Everything else is in sentences; part means region in sents[14].

Facts checked: spring has 6 solar terms, solar terms are based on the sun's position, lightning is seen before thunder is heard, and Auckland has winter in July.

units.key: Why should we learn about the Earth?

grammar.title: There be 句型（某地有……）
grammar.tip: 说“某地有……”用 There is / There are：一个或不可数的（水、塑料）用 is，两个及以上用 are；否定在 is / are 后加 not，问句把 is / are 放到 there 前面。问数量：How many + 复数 + are there? How much + 不可数 + is there? 例：There aren't many trees here. How many planets are there? — There are eight.

talk.name: Ranger Ray
talk.persona: You are Ranger Ray, a friendly park ranger on Echo Island who looks after the sea, the beaches and the forests. You are making a fact file about protecting the Earth for the island school, and you want the student's ideas for it.

units.notes: Unit 4, The Earth. FIXES APPLIED: (1) file vs fact file: both reviewers flagged this, and the two fixes partly conflict. I went with the game-format version: file = 档案 and fact file = 事实档案 (事实档案 is one of the textbook's own glosses). 事实 cues the word "fact" in 看图说英语, and the two meanings no longer read as the same thing in 听音选义. Sentence 16's Chinese keeps the more natural 资料档案, which is the textbook's other gloss. (2) The grammar tip now covers the negative (there isn't / there aren't) and How many + plural + are there / How much + uncountable + is there, which dlgs 1, 2 and 4 test. It says "two or more" take are instead of 好几个. I kept it shorter than the reviewer's draft so it fits the one-or-two-sentence limit. (3) sents[1] is now "There aren't many trees near our school." / 我们学校附近的树不多。 This adds a negative there-be sentence and matches the talk opener and chunk. 'amazing' still appears in dlg 6 as a wrong reply. (4) sents[9] Chinese: the reviewer's suggested 地下水里含有有害的化学品 still has the doubled 有有, so I used 地下水中含有害的化学品。 instead (含有害 as in the standard 含有害物质). (5) dlg 8 (sea quiz): the wrong replies are now "It covers only a small area." and "There are no animals in it.", which are on topic but factually wrong; 'area' is now used. (6) dlg 11: the wrong reply is now "To make the desert bigger." in place of the nonsense plastic option. NOT APPLIED: the 'must' fix to replace "provide ... with ..." with "provide us with". The task and schema require every official word and phrase to appear exactly once with exact spelling, and the official list (book/unit4.json) spells it "provide ... with ...". Renaming it would drop an official item and add an unofficial one. Chinese class dictation also asks for this exact form (为……提供…… → provide ... with ...). The no-"..." rule in the brief covers sentences and lines, and the full chunk is practised in sents 6, "Trees provide us with fresh air." Suggestion for the engine (not content): when speaking a word item, replace "..." with a short comma pause for TTS, and ignore the dots when scoring speech, so the child says "provide with". CHECKS (re-run against book/unit4.json): the 38 words + 11 phrases are all present exactly once, in book order, spelled exactly; there are no duplicate emoji or zh, and every zh is 8 characters or fewer. 🪐 🪓 🤲 need Unicode 12. All 16 sents are 6 to 10 words with no repeated word, so word-order questions have one answer. The passive "Too many trees are cut down every year." keeps "cut down" from being split. Grammar coverage: 7 of the 16 sents use there be (1, 2 negative, 3, 5, 7, 10, 12 How many), and dlgs 1 to 6 cover Is there / Are there / How many / How much and the short answers, including there isn't. Player-world items: sents 15 (Echo Mountain), dlg 5 (Echo Island), the boss line and Nova. Dlg 12 is the key question. Only in the word list, not in sents or dlgs: billion, grain, reach, website, own, emperor, war, blow, blow away, what's more ('what's more' is a talk chunk). The talk opener asks about trees at school, not home, so it collects no personal info.

units.key: What is it like to travel in space?

grammar.title: 一般将来时（will / be going to）

units.notes:
Unit 5 Off to space (飞向太空), source unit5.json. I checked the words list against the file with a script: all 36 official words and 5 phrases are there exactly once, in book order (41 items), each emoji is a single grapheme, no emoji is used twice, and every Chinese gloss is 8 characters or fewer. There are 16 sents (7 to 10 words each, all Chinese translations different) and 12 dlgs (every correct reply is 10 words or fewer, each has 2 wrong replies).

FIXES APPLIED:
(1) MUST, boss: Inky the octopus was replaced. The name is close to the Pokémon Inkay and the 🐙 emoji is already used by the boss Doctor Octo (data.js line 106). The new boss is 🐇 月兔船长 'Captain Bun, the moon rabbit'. The moon rabbit is public-domain folklore and links to sents[12] about ancient poems. No boss in data.js uses 🐇, but I could not see the bosses of the other textbook units, so check that none of them also uses 🐇.
(2) grammar.tip was rewritten. will now covers prediction, intention (意愿) and quick decisions, and be going to also covers things you can see are about to happen. The tip now gives won't and the No answers. The full stop before the Chinese semicolon is gone.
(3) dlgs[2]: the wrong reply 'I'm going to stay for a week.' became 'I'm going there next month.' (it answers When). Both reviewers asked for this.
(4) sents[5] became 'You won't need a spacesuit inside the space station.' This adds won't. It is true: astronauts wear normal clothes inside the station.
(5) introduction is now 引言；序言, the textbook's meaning.
(6) century emoji is now ⏳ instead of 💯 (Chinese students read 💯 as full marks).
(7) Engine fix, done in this run: in D:/Claude/echo-island/game.js line 356 I added kilometre(s)→kilometer(s), metre(s)→meter(s) and programme(s)→program(s) to the SPELL map, with a Chinese comment. The edit only adds entries and passes node --check. I did NOT run npm test. neighbour→neighbor was not added because they differ by one letter, which tokEq already accepts.

REVIEWER FIXES I CHANGED, AND WHY:
- sents[1]: the reviewer suggested 'We are going to leave for the Moon at nine.' That has the same problem the reviewer pointed out: 'leave at nine for the Moon' is also an acceptable order. I used 'We are going to leave for the Space Museum.' / 我们打算出发去太空博物馆。 instead. The subject is a person, there is one destination and no time phrase that can move, and it links to the textbook speaking activity 'A trip to the Space Museum' and to dlgs[0].
- sents[12]: the reviewer said 'Some ancient poems express a dream of flying to the Moon.' was 10 words, but it is 11. I used 'Some ancient poems express a dream of reaching the Moon.' (10 words) / 一些古诗表达了登上月亮的梦想。

COVERAGE:
- 9 sents practise will, won't or be going to (indexes 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 13). 8 dlgs practise the grammar (0 to 5, 8, 10). Each answer matches the helper verb (Will you / Yes, I will; Are you going to / Yes, I am) or the question word.
- Wrong replies use the wrong helper verb, the past tense, or answer a different question word.
- 'do exercise' is no longer in sents. It is still in dlgs[3], dlgs[7] and the talk words.
- Repeated words inside a sentence: 'the' in sents 3, 10 and 15, and 'of' in sents 11. The repeated tiles are the same word, so there is still only one correct order.
- These words appear only in the words list: tie, low, facility, pass, chance, introduction, experience, determination, already, neighbour, circle, release, programme. prepare appears only in 'prepare for' (dlgs[3]), experiment only as 'experiments' (dlgs[2]), and island only inside 'Echo Island' (dlgs[0] and [4]).

units.key: How do we introduce a city or town?

units.notes:
I checked the word list against unit6.json. It has all 33 official words and all 6 official phrases, each once, in book order. 'historic' is a recognition-only word: it stays in the list, and the phrase 'historic site' carries it in sentence 11.

Fixes applied:
(1) sight. Both reviewers flagged it. I chose '视力；看见' over '看见（名词）'. The bracketed label looks odd as an answer option, while 视力 is a natural noun meaning that clearly tells the child to say 'sight' and not 'see'. The textbook's 看见 is kept as the second meaning.

- sents[6]: We had a charity sale at school last month became Our school had a charity sale last month, because at school and last month could swap.
- sents[7]: We sold apple pies and raised fifty dollars became We raised fifty dollars by selling apple pies, because the two halves joined by and could swap. This is the same problem the reviewer flagged in sents[11].
- sents[12]: I competed in the long jump on sports day became On sports day I competed in the long jump, because the two prepositional phrases could swap.

The Chinese translations of these sentences stay the same apart from sents[7]: 我们靠卖苹果派筹到了五十美元。 sents[12] and sents[15] both contain 运动会, but one is about 跳远 and the other is about 一年一度, so they are still easy to tell apart.

The only repeated words in the word-order sentences are the two the tiles in sents[11] and sents[13]. They are interchangeable because game.js compares lowercase text, so this is safe. 12 of the 16 sentences use the simple past: regular -ed verbs (launched, acted, raised, decorated, competed), irregular verbs (went, became, had, ate, fell, made) and one Did-question. 9 of the 12 dialogues use the past.

The rest of the earlier design stays the same. The Chinese meanings are kept apart: definitely is 肯定；确实 and of course is 当然; join is 加入（社团）, attend is 出席；参加 and compete is 参加比赛. The emoji are kept apart too: fair is 🎡 and clubs fair is 🎪. The boss is an otter because the octopus is already used by the Subjects island. The talk character is not called Nina because Nurse Nina already exists.

grammar.title: 人称代词与物主代词
grammar.tip: 做主语用 I / he / she / they，放在动词或介词后面用 me / him / her / them。my / your / her 后面一定要跟名词，mine / yours / hers 后面不跟名词：This is my coin. The coin is mine. 问“谁的”用 whose：Whose stamps are these? They're hers.

talk.name: Grandpa Joe
talk.persona: You are Grandpa Joe, a kind old sailor on Echo Island. You have collected stamps, coins and shells from all over the world, and you keep them in a small collection room at the island museum. You love hearing what young people collect.
talk.goal: The student tells Grandpa Joe what they collect (or would like to collect), about how many they have got, and one reason why they like collecting it, and uses at least one possessive word such as my, mine or yours.
talk.goalZh: 告诉乔爷爷你收藏（或想收藏）什么、大概有多少、为什么喜欢收藏，并且至少用一次 my / mine / yours 这样的物主代词。
talk.opener: Hello there! I'm Grandpa Joe. Do you collect anything?

units.notes:
Source: C:/Users/Frank/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--Claude/073ac0e8-fd7f-4d6a-954a-c072b256e3ed/scratchpad/book/unit8.json. I re-checked the words list with the script scratchpad/u8chk.js. It has 41 entries: the 36 official words and the 5 phrases, each once, in book order, with the book's spelling. There is one deliberate exception. The official phrase "add ... to ..." is stored as "add to" (a MUST fix). The TTS voice would read the dots aloud, and speech recognition could never match the literal string. Any script that checks spelling against the book should treat "add to" as that phrase. The sentence "I want to add these stickers to my album." practises the full add ... to ... pattern. Every emoji is a single character, every Chinese gloss is 8 characters or fewer, and no gloss or emoji appears twice.

FIXES APPLIED:
(1) item and object, where the two reviewers' fixes conflicted. item is now 一件商品；一项 🛍️. This follows the textbook's own gloss (一件商品（或物品）), so it matches what the class is taught, and 一项 keeps the "one thing on a list" sense. object is now 物体 🏺. The two glosses no longer share any meaning. I did not use the English-lens gloss 一件；一项 alone, because it is too abstract for a 12-year-old.
(2) Boss: Inky is a Pac-Man ghost, so the boss is renamed Pockets. The name is invented and echoes pocket money. The Chinese name 章鱼收藏家 is kept.
(3) sents[4]: I used neither reviewer's version, because each still has a word that can move. In "I like to add new stickers to my album", "new" can move to "my new album". In "I often add stickers to my album", "often" can move to the end. Both would make the word-order task wrong for a correct answer. Final sentence: "I want to add these stickers to my album." It has no movable adjective or adverb, and the two "to" tokens are the same string, so swapping them changes nothing.
(4) sents[12]: possible near-copy of the reading passage (own, impossible, single, every stamp), so it is replaced with "It was almost impossible to find this stamp." / 找到这张邮票几乎是不可能的。 As a result, own, single, absolutely, seem, nail, item and real appear only in the word drills.
(5) dlgs[8]: the wrong reply "No, I've got about fifty" is replaced with "No, I keep them in my bedroom." A child could hear "fifty" as an amount of money.
(6) dlgs[10]: the two "time" puns are replaced with plausible but clearly wrong replies. I used "sixty" instead of the reviewer's "two hundred", because "two hundred" would repeat the correct answer of dlgs[7].

EXTRA ORDER-TASK FIXES (same problem the reviewers found):
- sents[1]: "real" could move ("stories about the real past"), so it is now "Stamps can unlock stories about the past."
- sents[10]: "lovely" could move ("This lovely chocolate bar wrapper has a pattern"), so it is now "This chocolate bar wrapper has a star pattern."
- The grammar tip is now split into clearer sentences, with the same content.

Some sentences are yes/no questions, for example "Is this old envelope yours?". Their words could also form a statement, but the order-task audio makes the intended order clear. I left these as normal listening items.

COVERAGE:
- Grammar: 11 of 16 sentences and 6 of 12 dialogues practise my/his/her/our, mine/yours/hers, it vs them and me vs him. The wrong replies in those dialogues are deliberate pronoun mistakes. The other dialogues' wrong replies answer a different question word.
- Textbook sections: sents[13] covers the History part (money in different forms), sents[14] and [11] cover the survey and the opinion part of the speaking task, and sents[15] covers the online-museum project.
- Boss and chat character are original.
